result.headline: In this 5-minute run the GA scored a test mean of 30.49 apples against 26.51 for DQN, but DQN reached its score with about 80 times fewer game steps (391k vs 30.8M).
result.summary:
**GA** (a population of 200 networks that breed and mutate, with no gradients) had the higher test mean, 30.49 apples (median 32, best 38). It played long games: 729 steps per game, or 24 steps per apple. Most games ended by hitting its own body (85), with 10 wall crashes and 5 starvations, where the snake loops without eating. Its training curve climbed steadily from about 0.1 to about 17 in mean_last_100 by roughly minute 3.8, then wobbled (17.6, 12.6, 16.7). That wobble is normal GA noise: each generation is a fresh population, so the score depends partly on which generation the lab looks at. The GA ran about 103k steps per second on 11 cores and finished 78,000 games.

**DQN** (a neural network that learns the value of each move from stored experience, with exploration) reached a test mean of 26.51 (median 26, best 42). It played short, efficient games: 233 steps per game, or 9 steps per apple. It died mostly by body collisions (76) and walls (24), never by starvation. Its training curve rose quickly, from about 1.5 at minute 0.5 to about 17.6 at minute 1.4, then flattened near 19 to 21. Its training mean of 19.15 is lower than its test mean because training still includes random exploratory moves. DQN ran at only about 1.3k steps per second and got through 391k steps in 5 minutes.
result.diagnosis:
The window vision (radius 2) shows each snake only the 5x5 squares around its head, plus the apple direction. That is enough for DQN to head for apples efficiently (9 steps per apple), but it cannot see a long body or a far wall coming, which fits DQN dying mostly by body collisions. The GA does not need quick decisions: with the starve penalty (10) and the small hunger cost (0.01) it can take a slow, careful route, which gives 24 steps per apple. The per-move hunger penalty is small, so it only mildly pushes the GA toward eating sooner; that explains why only 5 games starved.

DQN's gap is mostly speed. The potential reward (0.1) gives it a distance-based hint each move, which helps learning, but 391k steps is far too few for it to keep improving much. The GA's larger total reach here comes from having 79 times more steps, not from a better method per step. Caution: this run was 5 minutes, while the baseline lessons were 10 minutes, and it changed both vision and reward from the scratch rays run, so the comparison with those runs is confounded. It is also a single seed. The 4-point gap between GA and DQN should be judged against the spread across seeds, which we do not have yet.
result.learned: A higher test score does not mean a more efficient agent: the GA beat DQN on score in this 5-minute run, but DQN was far more efficient per game step, and the comparison depends on whether you measure per step or per minute. Also check how each game ended (wall, body, starved): a high score with many starvations and long games means something different from a high score with short games.

recommendations.title: Try rays vision with this reward
recommendations.why: Window vision sees only two squares around the head, and DQN dies mostly by body collisions. Rays look further along eight lines, which may let DQN avoid its own body earlier.
recommendations.change: Switch the vision from window radius 2 to rays with depth 4, keeping the reward, algorithms and 5-minute budget the same.
recommendations.prediction: DQN test mean moves by more than 3 points, most likely up to 28 to 32, and its body-collision share falls below 70 percent of test games; the GA changes less than DQN.
recommendations.question: Does longer sight along lines help DQN avoid its body more than a 5x5 picture of the squares around the head?

recommendations.title: Remove the hunger penalty
recommendations.why: Hunger (0.01 per move) is the only pressure against slow, looping play for the GA. If it is what keeps GA starvation low at 5 of 100 games, removing it should let the GA wander more.
recommendations.change: Remove the hunger feature from the reward and keep apple, death, starve and potential at their current values.
recommendations.prediction: GA test steps per game rise above 800 and its starved count rises above 5 of 100 games; DQN changes by less than 3 points.
recommendations.question: Is the small per-move hunger cost what keeps the GA from looping forever?

recommendations.title: Repeat this lesson with seed 1
recommendations.why: The GA-DQN gap of about 4 points comes from one seed. A second seed shows whether the ranking holds or was luck.
recommendations.change: Keep every setting the same and change only the seed from 0 to 1.
recommendations.prediction: GA test mean stays within about 3 points of 30.5 and DQN within about 3 points of 26.5, so GA stays ahead by a similar margin.
recommendations.question: Does the GA finishing ahead of DQN in test score hold on a second seed?

ideas.title: Seed-group spread on test scores
ideas.what: Show the test mean with its spread (min, max, or standard deviation) across several seeds of the same recipe on the results table, so a single seed cannot be read as a ranking.
ideas.why: The GA and DQN test means differ by about 4 points on one seed, and the training curves wobble by 4 to 5 points between checkpoints, so the lab cannot tell noise from effect here.
ideas.expected: Lets learners see whether a gap is bigger than the seed-to-seed spread, which is usually a few points for these runs.

ideas.title: DQN train-every-N-steps setting
ideas.what: Add a setting for how often DQN takes a gradient update (for example one update per 4 environment steps), so the agent can spend less time training and more time collecting experience per second.
ideas.why: DQN ran at about 1.3k steps per second and collected only 391k steps in 5 minutes, while the GA collected 30.8M. Its curve was still rising at minute 1.4 and then flattened, so more experience per minute may help it.
ideas.expected: Several times more environment steps per minute for DQN, which could raise its test mean by a few points within the same 5-minute budget.
